title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
The page is a re-used sheet. The upside-down typescript is page IX-110 of the typescript of SGA 7, Exposé IX (Grothendieck, 'Modèles de Néron et monodromie'), section 9.4. Its scratch-paper side carries a few handwritten fragments belonging to the 1975–76 notes on the divided-power de Rham complex.

**The typescript: Lemma 9.4.3.** It is a lemma on cohomological duality over a strictly local trait.
- **Setting.** S is the spectrum of a strictly henselian discrete valuation ring V, with generic point η = Spec K. Λ is a finite coefficient ring. Q and P are Λ_S-modules (or Λ-module schemes), Q locally free of finite type. ∨ denotes Hom(-, Q/Z) and D denotes Cartier duality Hom(-, G_m).
- **(a)** Ext^i_Λ(Q,P) ≅ H^i(S, Q̌⊗P), and similarly on η. This holds because Q is locally free, so Ext reduces to cohomology of the internal Hom, Q̌⊗P.
- **(b)** A canonical identification of Q̌⊗P with a Cartier dual.
- **(c)** For a finite constant group H, H^i(S, D(H)) = H^i(η, D(H)_η) = 0 for i ≥ 2.
- **(d)** H^1(S, D(H)) ≅ V*⊗Ȟ_o and H^1(η, D(H)) ≅ K*⊗Ȟ_o.
- **Proof of (c) and (d).** Reduce to H_o = Z/m, so D(H) = μ_m. Use the Kummer sequence 0 → μ_m → G_m → G_m → 0 (exact for the fppf topology, which is needed when p divides m). This reduces everything to H^i(S, G_m) = H^i(η, G_m) = 0 for i ≥ 1.
  - Smooth group schemes have the same flat and étale cohomology (Brauer III, th. 11.7). On a strictly local S the étale cohomology vanishes in positive degree.
  - On η, H^1(K, G_m) = 0 by Hilbert 90. Br(K) = 0 for the fraction field of a strictly henselian DVR (cited as [6, th. 1.1]). Higher groups vanish by cohomological dimension (more care is needed at p in characteristic p).
  - Then H^1(μ_m) = G_m/m, giving (d).
- **Purpose.** This feeds Grothendieck's pairing / orthogonality theorems for Néron models and component groups in SGA 7 IX.

**The handwritten margin.** It contains fragmentary notes:
- something like 'H^i(S)_n = (S_n)…';
- a map 'u: V(C_n)^n → V(C)…';
- 'V(C−n)', 'V''(C…)'.

These apparently belong to the graded comodule / divided-power algebra discussion of the previous page (graded S-comodules versus locally nilpotent graded S^h-modules). They are too fragmentary to reconstruct, and a blue stroke crosses them out.
errors: In (d), the second formula is typed as G_m(η)⊗H_o, then as K*⊗Ȟ_o. The dual Ȟ_o is intended, consistent with the first formula; this is a minor typo.
In (b), 'D(Q⊗Q*)' is most likely a typo or misreading for something like D(Q⊗P*), since the left side Q̌⊗P involves P.

The Kummer sequence with m divisible by the residue characteristic requires the fppf topology. The proof implicitly uses flat cohomology together with the comparison theorem (Brauer III 11.7); this is fine but left implicit.
The vanishing of H^i(η, G_m) for i ≥ 2 at the p-part in characteristic p is not fully justified by Br(K) = 0 alone. It is standard, but compressed into one citation.

ideas.what: Ext of locally free Λ-modules equals cohomology of the dual tensor; vanishing of H^i of μ_m (i ≥ 2) and H^1 = units⊗dual over a strictly local trait and its generic point, via the Kummer sequence and Br(K) = 0
ideas.modern_name: Kummer theory / flat cohomology of μ_m over strictly henselian DVRs; Cartier duality
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (SGA 7 IX); Brauer group results from Lang / Grothendieck Brauer III

ideas.what: Handwritten fragments on graded objects V(C_n) → V(C), likely related to divided-power / comodule structures

deep.surprise_reason: The typescript is a published page of SGA 7 IX reused as scratch paper. The handwritten notes are crossed-out, illegible fragments with no recoverable new content.
transcription_corrections: The typescript is printed upside down and is a reused SGA 7 Exposé IX page (page IX-110), not part of the de Rham notes.
In (d), the second isomorphism should read H^1(η, D(H_η)) ≃ G_m(η)⊗Ȟ_o = K*⊗Ȟ_o.
In (b), the right-hand side is likely D(Q⊗P*) rather than D(Q⊗Q*); verify against the image or the published SGA 7 text.
